In the workplace, one of the most common challenges for employers is the fact that you may have too many things to do and not enough time to complete these tasks. In order for you to get things done, you will need to delegate and also accept responsibilities that are given to you. Here's some language for delegating and accepting responsibilities.

Example: She will review your progress at the end of each day.

Example: Please confirm your acceptance of this assignment.
a ​statement, often written, that something is certain or true
Example: This e-mail is a confirmation in regards to the assignment for Thursday.
Example: You will write this proposal on behalf of Polygon.
to tell someone what you think they should do
Example: It is advised that you meet with Miranda.
Imagine you receive an e-mail from your boss. She/he has tasked you with writing an agenda for a staff meeting.
You have to write a response back to your boss letting her/him know that you have accepted the responsibility she/he have given you.
Remember to use the correct format and formal language.

images.text:
Subject: Important: Assignment for this Thursday

Hello Peter,

You are aware that Polygon is intending to expand its market into South America. The competition is fierce but we have the attention of Farmani. As we requested, he has extended the proposal deadline for a bid to promote Holly's clothing line to this Friday. I am commissioning you to write the proposal.

Please consult with Miranda Morehouse if you have any questions. I have asked her to review your progress at the end of each day. The assignment must be completed by Thursday at noon.

Would you please reply to this e-mail to confirm your acceptance of this assignment and its deadline? I am confident in your abilities.

Regards,
Janet Ellison, CEO
Polygon

______________________________

Subject: Confirmation of Assignment for Thursday

Dear Miss Ellison,

I am writing to confirm my acceptance of the assignment to write the proposal to Farmani on behalf of Polygon. As advised, I will consult with Miranda Morehouse and review my progress at the end of each day.

You may be sure that I will have the proposal finished with excellence by noon on Thursday. Thank you for your confidence and this opportunity to contribute at an exciting time!

Sincerely,
Peter Smith

Writing a Business E-mail

  • Use a professional e-mail address.
  • Write a short subject (6-8 words).
  • Start with a salutation (use names and titles).
  • Explain the reason for writing the e-mail.
  • Be concise.
  • Break the message into paragraphs.
  • End with a closing
